newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling eases vs dollar after intervention.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling eases vs dollar after intervention.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was a touch weaker against the dollar on Wednesday after the central bank bought dollars at 54 shillings, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.89 to the dollar from 53.88 on Tuesday, while against the pound sterling it was posted at 88.15 from 87.35.
Dealers said the market appeared to have stabilised at the 53.70/54.10 level.
"Although it's happening cautiously, spreads have shrunk to 30 (cents) and maybe next week they will be at 10," said a dealer from one leading commercial bank.
The central bank intervention was the first for a month and bank chief economist Maurice Kanga said it was needed to stop the shilling from appreciating to the 52 level too fast.
"It's very hard to say exactly what will happen to the shilling definitely, one can only guess the direction. It still looks like the shilling is threatening to strengthen," he added.
The money market was tight. Overnight rates were between 19 and 20 percent compared to between 13 and 16 percent on Tuesday.
